title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting + streaming stability fixes
author: Ava Patel
description: This PR brings the Redwood OpenAI-compat /v1/chat.completions surface closer to parity with the OpenAI reference by addressing: 1) parameter alignment (temperature, top_p, n, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, max_tokens mapping), 2) role handling and strict role validation to match chat semantics, 3) support for stop sequences and returning logprobs when requested, 4) response formatting improvements for deterministic structured output, and 5) streaming stability fixes for function/tool calls and chunk framing. Motivation: downstream customers expect drop-in compatibility for popular SDKs and existing prompts. Without parity we see subtle behavior drift (role normalization, truncated stop handling, inconsistent logprob payloads, and intermittent streaming resets during high concurrency). This change set is intentionally scoped to the API surface and request/response translation layer; no model weights or runtime kernel changes are made here. Summary of changes included below. Checklist: - [x] Map OpenAI params to internal runtime config with documented fallbacks - [x] Ensure roles (user/system/assistant/tool) are preserved and validated - [x] Implement stop sequence handling with multi-stop support and correct truncation semantics - [x] Emit logprobs payload when logprobs requested (token-level + top_logprobs) - [x] Normalize JSON response formatting for structured output endpoints - [x] Harden streaming iterator to avoid resets during backpressure and function-call transitions - [x] Add unit + integration tests (API compatibility suite + streaming conformance) - [x] Update docs and changelog (redwood-docs openai compatibility section) Related: ENG-4107 (streaming flakes incident), PM-913 (compat parity spec), previous PRs that iterated on chat parity.
commits: Map OpenAI params to internal config and add conversion tests
Validate roles and add role-preserving deserializer
Stop sequences: implement multi-stop truncation and tests
Logprobs: add token-level logprob serialization and top_logprobs
Streaming: stabilize chunk framing & resume logic for function/tool calls

notes: Motivation and customer impact described in PM-913; parity reduces migration cost for customers using OpenAI-compatible SDKs.
This PR intentionally keeps runtime execution semantics unchanged; only the API translation layer and streaming iterator behaviour were updated.
We limit 'n' to 5 at the mapping layer to prevent accidental high-cost loops from naive client code; product agreed on this guard in PM-913.
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity updates: parameter mapping (temperature/top_p/n/max_tokens), strict role preservation, multi-stop support, logprobs returned when requested, improved streaming stability for function/tool calls and structured responses. No breaking changes expected for most clients; minor guard applied to 'n' (capped at 5).
